title: Uniform microsupport and the natural dual source
reviewed_arguments: All 23 original obligations, 29 displays and three complete solutions remain. The two exercise prose corrections are recorded explicitly.

Zero extension identifies the Dirichlet form space with supported H1 by equality of norms on compact interior approximants and supported density. The earlier complete weak-H1 proof identifies the Neumann space with restricted H1.

The exact antidual theorem represents the Neumann source by supported H−1, including boundary terms, and the Dirichlet source by restricted H−1. Higher-order transpose actions use the actual smooth test spaces and quotient ideal.
The weighted adjoint is J inverse times the Lebesgue adjoint times J. Every local coefficient bound and form-domain preservation follows by the product rule, positivity and compact support.
Compact localizer kernels are distinguished from proper auxiliary parametrices and the full identity. Proper projections give fixed input/output cutoffs for every norm estimate.

Uniform microsupport uses all derivative rapid-decay bounds and the resolved residual topology. Finite-cover ordered composition proves separated products in both orders, every target remainder and the fixed elliptic tester equivalence.

The left parametrix gives the exact negative residual term in the single-tester identity; order-zero bounds and actual adjoints establish membership and norms on both form spaces and antiduals for every real order.

The finite-cover tester retains each operator order and uses all-real inverse lower bounds in the full symbol quotient. Nonclassical symbols do not acquire a false homogeneous unit-cosphere representative.
Every individual regularizer has nonpositive order. The family may be bounded only in the target order s; these conditions have different roles.

The half-order split uses an actual right parametrix, the actual adjoint and the negative residual term. The source orders s plus one half and s are distinct; absorption has precisely C_A squared over four epsilon.

The periodic H1 and antidual sequence identifications follow from the complete earlier circle basis. Uniform kernel periodization proves the pseudodifferential family interpretation of the finite-rank counterexample.

The exact circle examples show nonempty uniform microsupport, necessity of the tester order, both weighted Fourier bounds and failure of the lowered source product estimate even with bounded bare norms.
The shrinking multiplier has its exact derivative lower bound and valid product-rule upper bound. An explicit Hilbert functional attains the needed norm; no undeclared Hahn–Banach theorem is used.
The two-scale estimate retains all finite symbol and residual constants and their squaring under absorption, without claiming compensated glancing constants.
The figure labels possible open bands, exact center modes, exact-formula samples and the unit weighted norms. Numerical samples supplement the proofs.

Vasy and Melrose were checked in their exact admitted PDFs, including visual inspection of both page-20 statements. Melrose leaves the family lemma as an exercise; the lesson supplies its full energy/dual proof.
